name: tab-bar
summary: The bar of tabs at the bottom of a phone screen: two to five of an app's top-level pages, each an icon over a short label, with the current one marked.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Names the navigation for screen readers; not shown.

properties.name: current
properties.description: The label of the item that is the current page.

slots.name: items
slots.description: Two to five tabs: a short label and an icon each. The icon is decorative; the label names the tab.

slots.name: accessory
slots.description: One optional item that sits apart in a circle of its own at the end of the bar, such as Search. Only its icon shows; its label names it for screen readers.

events.name: press
events.description: A tab or the accessory is pressed, with its label.

states.name: rest
states.description: Muted icon and label; the current tab in the accent colours on an accent wash.

states.name: focused
states.description: A ring around the focused tab.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The tab scales to the press scale, never under reduced motion.

accessibility.name: Its label names the navigation; each tab by its label, never its icon; the current one marked.
accessibility.keyboard: Each tab is its own tab stop; Enter and Space press it.
accessibility.web: A <nav> named by its label, of links named by their labels, the current one with aria-current="page"; icons are aria-hidden.
accessibility.apple: A container named by its label, of buttons named by their labels with the selected trait on the current one; icons are hidden from VoiceOver.
accessibility.windows: A UI Automation ControlType.List named by its label, of ListItems named by their labels with SelectionItem, the current one selected, like a NavigationView's top-level items.
accessibility.android: A selectableGroup named by its label, of NavigationBarItem nodes with Role.Tab, the selected state on the current one and a click action, named by their labels; icons carry no content description.

cases.person: Three icons over short words along the bottom, Recipes on an accent wash, and a Search circle apart at the end.
Two icons over short words, Home on an accent wash.

deviations: Web's items are links (href, paths) and the current one follows currentPath; native kits take a current label and a press handler, as an app navigates itself.
Web hides it from a breakpoint and slides it away under the on-screen keyboard (hideFrom); native bars leave both to the platform.
Drawn rather than the system's TabView bar, so it matches web's accent wash; its tabs are buttons with the selected trait.
A bottom bar is not a Windows pattern: on a desktop the app uses Sidebar, which maps to NavigationView, and this bar only on a phone-sized window.
Drawn rather than Material's NavigationBar, to keep web's 64 dp height and accent wash; its items carry Role.Tab as NavigationBarItem's do.
